_comment: Drift-correction tool. AutoForm over DriftViewModel. Left: a single-column Settings dock in workflow order — load the image, pick the channel the drift is measured on, choose the reference and how the correction is applied. Right: the drift trace, the before/after projections that show whether it worked, and the per-frame shift table. Run / export live in the host toolbar; long help sits behind the ? button.

options.label: Image
options.description: The stack to correct: a TIFF stack, or a photon-stream file (PTU/HT3/…) reconstructed into a confocal-scan image. Photon streams are corrected photon by photon, so the result stays usable for lifetime and correlation analysis.

sections.label: Measure on
sections.description: Channel the drift is measured on. The sample moves as a whole, so one channel drives the estimate and the correction is applied to all of them. Pick the brightest, most structured channel — a flat, empty channel gives a soft correlation peak and an unreliable shift.

sections.label: Reference
sections.description: Which frame each frame is compared with. 'First frame' is right for slow monotonic drift and never accumulates error. 'Previous frame' follows non-monotonic wander but lets small per-frame errors add up over a long series. 'Stack mean' is a compromise for noisy data.

sections.label: Apply by
sections.description: Wrapping rolls the content that leaves one edge back in at the other, conserving every photon but making the wrapped strip meaningless. Blanking discards it and leaves the vacated strip empty — honest, but the edges then carry no signal. Wrapping matches the reference implementation.

sections.label: Smoothing (σ px)
sections.description: Gaussian blur applied to the correlation before the peak is located. Guards against a noise-driven tie between two neighbouring pixels flipping the answer by one pixel. Zero disables it.

sections.label: Sub-pixel refinement
sections.description: Refine each integer peak by fitting a parabola through its neighbours. Useful for slow drift measured over many frames; the correction itself is still applied in whole pixels.

sections.title: Drift trace
sections.description: Measured displacement per frame. A straight line is stage drift; a jump is a bump or a refocus; noise around zero means there was nothing to correct.

sections.title: Before
sections.description: All frames summed before correction. Drift shows up here as a directional blur.

sections.title: After
sections.description: The same projection after correction. If the correction worked, features are sharper here than on the left; if the two look identical, there was no drift to remove.
